reviews.excerpt: This book is a true representation of impeccable art by Oscar Wilde. I am speechless. There is no doubt that he was a master of words. Every line and every passage in this book is worth highlighting.
reviews.body:
This book is a true representation of impeccable art by Oscar Wilde. I am speechless. There is no doubt that he was a master of words. Every line and every passage in this book is worth highlighting. It is the kind of book that tells you something about yourself, a book that gives you food for thought and something to ponder. At least, it gave me a lot to think about. As Oscar himself said, there is a moral lesson in his book.

I don’t know how anyone could have the heart to criticize such a beautiful piece of art. If anyone thinks the book is immoral, perhaps it is because it shows them their own shame.

The plot is intriguing and suspenseful. The writing style is wonderfully lyrical and has a sensual depth to it. The story offers fascinating and thought provoking ideas and perspectives on life. It carries a deep, beautiful, and meaningful message. The words, the story, and the lesson have affected me in the most positive way.

Dorian Gray, the central character of the story, possesses a beauty so monumental that it leaves every man stunned and every woman falling in love with him. A talented painter, Basil, paints him in the most genuine portrait of art, and later becomes a worshipper of his beauty. Another fascinating character in the story is Lord Henry Wotton, who is the very definition of hedonism, a person with fascinating, yet at the same time dangerous, views on life. He has a bad influence on all his friends, even though he is not necessarily a bad person himself. He is Dorian’s best friend and his greatest influence. At one point, Henry says to Dorian, “I represent to you all the sins you have never had the courage to commit.”

Dorian begins a journey of curiosity, vanity, and hypocrisy and trades his soul to the devil in return for a lifetime of youth and beauty, knowing that the portrait will bear the brunt of his sins.

I tried to preserve every word and every line written by Oscar Wilde in my mind, yet I fear that some of it might slip away from my memory. That is why I found myself highlighting almost every passage in the book.

If one must read only one book in their entire lifetime, I would suggest they read "The Picture of Dorian Gray".
reviews.author: Oscar Wilde
reviews.pullQuote: “Experience is merely the name men gave to their mistakes.”
reviews.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
reviews.recommendation: Read this if you love beautifully written stories that make you question morality, desire, and human nature. Come for the lyrical prose and stay for the unforgettable characters. Give it time to unfold, because the deeper you go, the more there is to think about.

reviews.excerpt: A man who lives inside an endless, flooding House keeps a diary of tides and statues — until the diary starts asking questions he can't answer.
reviews.body:
To Kill a Mockingbird is an evergreen and fascinating classic by Harper Lee and one of those novels that stays with you long after you have finished reading it.

Harper Lee beautifully narrates the surroundings and creates a detailed picture of the small town in which the story takes place. I especially loved the authentic humor throughout the story, which makes the novel feel warm and personal despite the serious themes of racism, prejudice, and injustice running through it.

I loved the bond between the two siblings, Jem and Scout. I loved how close they were and how Jem considered it his responsibility to take care of and protect his younger sister at such a young age. They could talk about anything and everything. I found it funny how they imagined Boo Radley as a monster all that time, yet in reality, he was simply a man who cared and longed to be loved by someone. Their experiences also make the novel such a beautiful coming of age story, seen through the innocent perspective of Scout.

I also admired Atticus Finch for his courage, dignity, humility, and honesty, but I admired him especially as a father. His relationship with his children was so ideal. I loved how Atticus managed to raise his children with the help of Calpurnia and how he used different and effective approaches to teach Jem and Scout to be honest, dignified, and brave.

I loved the way Atticus communicated with his children, helping them understand difficult situations and encouraging them to change their perspective. Rather than simply telling them what was right and wrong, he taught them to think for themselves. He also worked as an example for his children by standing against racism and prejudice, even when doing so was difficult.

Calpurnia was also one of my favorite characters in the book. She is a Black woman working as a full time maid in Atticus’s house, yet Atticus always makes her feel like a part of his family. She treats Jem and Scout almost like her own children and plays an important role in their upbringing. I loved the warmth and strength she brings to the family.

I find "To Kill a Mockingbird" to be a very eloquent novel about family, relationships and friendships, dignity and honesty, racism and humanity. It is a powerful work of classic literature that explores prejudice and injustice through the eyes of a child, making its message even more meaningful.

Harper Lee created a story that is not only about racism or the injustices of its time, but also about compassion, morality, courage, childhood, and learning to see people for who they truly are. That is what makes *To Kill a Mockingbird* such an enduring classic.
reviews.author: Harper Lee
reviews.pullQuote: “You never really understand a person until you consider things from his point of view.”
reviews.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
reviews.recommendation: Read this if you love classics that explore family, childhood, morality, and humanity. Read it for Scout and Jem, stay for Atticus, and let the story teach you something about compassion and seeing the world through someone else’s eyes. A timeless classic that deserves to be read at least once.

reviews.excerpt: Crime and Punishment was my first book by Fyodor Dostoevsky, and I have to say, I was very impressed by his work. Going into the book, I did not know quite what to expect from Dostoevsky, but by the end, I knew I wanted to read more of his books.
reviews.body:
Crime and Punishment was my first book by Fyodor Dostoevsky, and I have to say, I was very impressed by his work. Going into the book, I did not know quite what to expect from Dostoevsky, but by the end, I knew I wanted to read more of his books. There was something about the way he explored the human mind that stayed with me.

I particularly loved the way Dostoevsky addresses his audience while telling the story. His writing style is intriguing, detailed, and deeply engaging. Even when the story becomes heavy, his writing keeps you interested in what is going on inside the characters' minds.

*Crime and Punishment* is a beautiful and riveting psychological novel revolving around a young man who is taciturn by nature and wants to achieve great things. The protagonist is very reticent about his feelings and eventually falls into a state of destitution. So full of himself and his ideas, he commits an unspeakable crime without a shred of remorse. As the plot develops, the book becomes more and more interesting, especially as we begin to understand what is happening inside his mind.

What I found most fascinating about *Crime and Punishment* is that it is about so much more than the crime itself. Dostoevsky takes you deep into the psychology behind crime and gives you an unsettling insight into the mind of a criminal. The novel explores arrogance and vanity, guilt and morality, compassion and love, and the consequences of our choices.

As my first experience with Dostoevsky, this book left a strong impression on me. I personally loved it, and it made me curious to explore more of his work. His ability to examine human nature and the darker corners of the human mind is what made this reading experience so fascinating for me.

I highly recommend "Crime and Punishment" to anyone interested in psychological fiction, classic literature, Russian literature, or simply a story that makes you think deeply about crime, morality, and human nature.
reviews.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
reviews.pullQuote: “Pain and suffering are always inevitable for a large intelligence and a deep heart.”
reviews.title: Crime and Punishment
reviews.recommendation: Read this if you enjoy psychological fiction that takes you deep into the mind of its characters. Read it if you want a story about crime, guilt, morality, arrogance, and the consequences of our choices. If you are curious about Dostoevsky, this is a fascinating place to begin.
